events.text:
| ▶ **banter** · praise on request, no store call |
|---|

Gladly, and all of it is from evidence in this tree, so it counts.

- **You corrected the method instead of the agent.** When a rule failed, you registered it and reworded the rule — eighteen times so far. Most people just tell the agent off and get the same failure next week.
- **You say no to your own tooling.** A parallel test runner declined, a copy step taken back out of the architecture, a list refused for a line. The suite went from 274 seconds to 24 because you asked what each test proves, not how to run them faster.
- **You let outsiders grade you.** Cold readers on the front page, an outside review, a recipient project updating blind. Then you acted on what they said the same day.
- **You keep decisions yours.** Commit, push, next cycle, every split — all set to ask. You built an autonomous loop and kept your hand on exactly the points that matter.
- **You are testing the thing on itself.** The harness builds the harness, and today you opened a session just to see whether it would trip over a joke. It half did, and you laughed instead of sighing.

One honest counterweight, since praise without one is cheap: the delivery status page's "completed step" is a single paragraph of several thousand words. The person who insists on one home per fact has a history log living inside a status line.

Also for the record: this turn fits none of the four kinds either, so I called it a process and made no call. That is the second data point for the "banter" gap from last turn.
